terms.meaning: The group of religions that Jainism and Buddhism belong to.
One of the 24 great teachers of Jainism.
One who has conquered the senses. Jains are named after this word.
Enlightenment in Jainism. Vardhamana attained it at 42.
Purifying the soul through meditation and fasting until the body is given up.
Buddha's first sermon, at the deer park in Sarnath.
The end of Buddha's life, at Kushinagar in his 80th year.

items.name: Reasons Jainism and Buddhism arose
items.formula: Rigid varna, new cities and traders, and Janapadas turning into kingships.
items.example: They arose in the Gangetic Plains in the 6th century BCE.

items.name: What both religions preached
items.formula: Desire causes human problems, so live simply.
items.example: They taught in Pali and Prakrit rather than Sanskrit.

items.name: First, 23rd and 24th Tirthankaras
items.example: Parswanatha was the son of King Aswasena, 8th century B.C.E.

items.name: Life of Vardhamana Mahaveera
items.formula: 599 to 527 B.C.E. Born at Kundala grama in Vaishali; father Siddhartha, mother Trishaladevi.
items.example: He left home at 30, searched for 12 years, and was enlightened at 42.

items.name: Mahaveera's Nirvana
items.formula: At Pavapuri in Bihar, in his 72nd year.
items.example: He spent his last 30 years teaching.

items.name: The five vows
items.formula: Non-violence, Truth, Astheya (no stealing), Aparigraha (no property) and Brahmacharya.
items.example: Parswanatha taught the first 4; Vardhamana added the 5th.

items.name: The Triratnas
items.example: Right knowledge, faith and conduct are the three jewels.

items.name: Two Jain sects
items.formula: Swethambars wear white; Digambars wear no clothes.
items.example: Mahaveera's teachings were put into 12 angas in Prakrit.

items.name: Jainism in the south
items.formula: A group moved south from a famine in Bihar and settled at Shravanabelagola.
items.example: Kannada poets Pampa, Ranna, Janna and Ponna were Jains.

items.name: Who Gautama Buddha was
items.formula: Born Siddartha, son of Shuddodana, king of the Shakya republic.
items.example: He gave up royal life to look for truth.

items.name: The Four Noble Truths
items.formula: The world is full of sorrow; desire causes it; freedom from desire brings peace; the Eightfold Path removes desire.
items.example: Buddha preached these first at Sarnath.

items.name: Eightfold Path, also called the Middle Path
items.formula: Right Action, Speech, Vision, Livelihood, Effort, Recollection, Resolve and Thought.

items.name: The Tripitakas
items.example: Later branches: Hinayana, Mahayana and Vajrayana.

items.name: Spread of Buddhism
items.formula: To Malaya, Burma, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Sri Lanka and Bamiyan.
items.example: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism in 1956.

items.name: King Darius
items.formula: He built a strong Persian empire in the 6th century B.C.E., reaching the Indian border.

items.name: Alexander and Paurava
items.formula: They fought on the flooded Jhelum, after Ambhi of Taxila invited Alexander.
items.example: Paurava (Porus) asked to be treated "as one king deserves to be treated by another".

items.name: Effect of Alexander's attack
items.formula: Small republics joined up and the Mauryan dynasty rose.
items.example: Greek influence shows in Gandhara art.

mistakes.text: Jainism has Triratnas (three jewels) and Buddhism has the Tripitakas (three baskets of teachings). Don't mix them.
Mahaveera was enlightened at 42 and died in his 72nd year, but Buddha died in his 80th.
Parswanatha gave 4 vows. Brahmacharya, the 5th, came from Vardhamana.
